Increase.description: A wealthy merchant from Maidens’ Delight who sets out on trading journeys with camels and bulls.

Lively.description: One of Increase's bulls, described as white, high-humped, and considered a good omen; he becomes separated from the group and thrives by the Jumna.

Rusty.description: The prideful and powerful lion king of the forest who rules over the animals, suffers from wounds or hunger, and is served by various counselors like jackals and leopards.

Victor.description: Cunning jackals and sons of counselors who serve the lion king Rusty, often conspiring together to manipulate forest politics.

The Loss of Friends.description: The title of Book I of the Panchatantra, focusing on the theme of friendship lost.

Maidens’ Delight.description: A city in the southern country, described as beautiful and prosperous.

Kailasa Peak.description: A sacred mountain in Hindu mythology, referenced to describe the city's shape.

Indrakila Mountain.description: A legendary mountain, used to describe the city's formidable portal.

Himalayas.description: The famous mountain range in northern India, referenced for the city's walls.

Mathura.description: An ancient city in India, destination of merchant Increase.

Jumna.description: A major river in northern India (modern Yamuna), where Lively recovers.

Shiva.description: A principal Hindu deity, referenced through the comparison to Shiva’s bull.

Circle of Four.description: A hierarchical structure of the lion’s court, consisting of four divisions.

asterism.description: A group of stars or a constellation, used here to denote an auspicious time.

conch-shell.description: A large shell used as a ceremonial trumpet in Indian culture.

grisleas.description: A type of tree found in Indian forests.

acacias.description: A type of tree common in India, known for its thorny branches.

dhaks.description: A species of tree native to India, also known as the flame-of-the-forest.

sals.description: A type of tree native to India, valued for its timber.

ant-hill.description: A mound built by ants, referenced as a metaphor and habitat.

banyan.description: A type of large fig tree native to India, known for its aerial roots.

understrappers.description: Subordinates or minor officials, used here for lower ranks in the lion’s court.

menials.description: Servants or those performing menial tasks, especially in a hierarchical society.

flyflap.description: A fan or implement used to drive away flies, often a symbol of royalty in India.

ichor.description: A fluid said to flow in the veins of gods, here referring to the liquid secreted by elephants.

flunkey.description: A servant or attendant, often used disparagingly for someone servile.

Vyasa.description: A saintly poet mentioned by Victor as the author of an epic poem about the Pandu princes.

Pandu princes.description: Legendary heroes from the Mahabharata, referenced in the context of entering Virata's court.

anjana-log.description: A type of wood mentioned as being split in the temple construction.

acacia-wood.description: A type of wood used for the wedge in the story.

Virata.description: A king whose court is referenced in connection with the Pandu princes.

Indus.description: A major river in the Indian subcontinent, used here as a poetic reference.

foreman.description: A supervisor or overseer of workers, especially in construction.

mechanic.description: In archaic usage, a skilled worker or craftsman.

doorkeeper.description: A person who guards or controls entry to a place, especially a palace or court.

reed of office.description: A ceremonial staff or symbol of authority held by a doorkeeper.

declasse.description: A French-derived term meaning of inferior social status or outcast.

conch-shells.description: Large sea shells used as trumpets in Indian rituals and ceremonies.

tambourines.description: Percussion instruments, often used in traditional music.

lutes.description: Stringed musical instruments, referenced in poetry.

chaplain.description: A clergyman attached to a royal court or household.

porter.description: A servant or attendant, especially one who carries luggage or guards a door.

functionary.description: A person who performs official duties, especially in a bureaucracy.

bureaucratic.description: Related to the administrative system governing any large institution.

dowager.description: A widow holding property or title from her deceased husband, often used for a queen mother.

prodigious.description: Remarkably or impressively great in extent, size, or degree.

serving-man.description: An archaic term for a male servant.

retainer.description: A servant or follower of a noble or royal household.

retinue.description: A group of attendants or followers accompanying an important person.

counselor.description: An advisor, especially one who gives advice to a king or ruler.

nectar.description: In Indian and classical literature, a divine or delightful drink, often symbolizing immortality or supreme pleasure.

bellowing.description: Making a loud, deep, roaring sound, as a bull or lion might do.

vehicle.description: In Hindu mythology, an animal or entity that serves as the mount or carrier of a deity.

Vidur.description: A wise counselor from the Indian epic Mahabharata, known for advising the blind king Dhritarashtra.

entourage.description: A group of attendants or associates, especially those accompanying a person of rank.

regaled.description: Entertained or treated to lavish enjoyment, especially with food or gifts.

cuffing.description: Striking with an open hand; a slap or blow.

roue.description: A debauched or dissipated man, often used in archaic English.

entree.description: The right to enter or join a particular sphere or group; access.

cajolery.description: Flattering or coaxing in order to persuade someone to do something.

clergy.description: The body of people ordained for religious duties, especially in the Christian Church.

amuck.description: A variant spelling of 'amok', meaning to behave uncontrollably and disruptively.

Godly.description: A holy man or wandering ascetic living in a monastery or hermitage who acquires wealth through offerings and is cautious about his treasure.

June.description: A rogue or naked monk who uses astronomical lore and trickery to plot against others or steal treasure.

monastery.description: A residence for monks or ascetics, often a place of religious retreat.

sacrifices.description: Ritual offerings made to deities, common in Hindu religious practice.

disciple.description: A follower or student of a religious teacher.

vow.description: A solemn promise, often of a religious nature.

ascetics.description: Individuals who practice severe self-discipline and abstain from worldly pleasures for spiritual reasons.

initiation.description: A ceremony or process by which someone is introduced into a religious group or practice.

robe.description: A long, loose garment worn by monks or ascetics.

thatch.description: A roofing material made from dried plant stalks, commonly used in rural India.

ram-fight.description: A specific event where two rams are fighting, serving as the central spectacle in the story.

fetters.description: Chains or shackles used to restrain someone, here used metaphorically to indicate being bound by desire.

ceremony of purification.description: A ritual act performed to cleanse oneself of impurity, often with religious or cultural significance.

lamentation.description: The passionate expression of grief or sorrow.

weaver.description: A craftsman who brings Godly home as a guest and is married to the unfaithful weaver's wife.

barber.description: The husband of the barber's wife, who is wrongly accused and punished for cutting off his wife's nose.

Krishna.description: A major deity in Hinduism, referenced in the context of traditional hospitality.

gunja-fruit.description: A reference to the seed of the Abrus precatorius plant, known for being attractive but poisonous.

devil-rain.description: A term for excessive rain, considered one of the eight kinds of devastation.

love-group.description: A classification of vices including drink, women, hunting, and dice.

wrath-group.description: A classification of vices including scolding, cruelty, and greed.

pious.description: Devoutly religious or showing reverence for the divine.

swain.description: An archaic term for a lover or suitor.

wench.description: An archaic or derogatory term for a young woman, often of low social status.

mollified.description: Soothed or calmed, especially after being angry.

adorer.description: One who loves or admires intensely.

impaled.description: A form of execution involving being pierced with a stake.

entrenchment.description: A defensive position or policy, often used metaphorically.

expedients.description: Means or methods used to achieve a particular end, often implying something done for convenience rather than principle.

crow.description: A pair of birds living in a banyan tree who suffer the loss of their chicks to a black snake.

black snake.description: A villainous black snake with a swelling hood that lives in a banyan tree and is eventually killed by the king's men.

heron.description: A bird mentioned in a story told by the jackal, who is ultimately killed by a crab.

crab.description: An animal in the jackal's story who kills the greedy heron.

chicks.description: Young birds, specifically the offspring of the crow and crow-hen.

baptism.description: A ceremonial act of initiation, here used metaphorically for the crow chicks' early stage of life.

villainous.description: Wicked or evil, used to describe the black snake.

venomous.description: Capable of injecting venom, describing the dangerous nature of the black snake.

device.description: A plan or scheme, often used in older English to mean a clever trick.

doom.description: Fate or destiny, often with a negative or fatal connotation.

indignant.description: Feeling or showing anger at unfair treatment, describing the crow's emotional state.

opportune.description: Suitable or favorable for a particular situation.

pond.description: A small body of still water.

nippers.description: Pincers or claws, especially those of a crab.

lotus-stalk.description: The stem of a lotus plant, often referenced in Indian literature.

chamberlains.description: High-ranking officials in the household of a monarch.

eunuchs.description: Castrated men, often employed as guards or servants in royal courts.

purblind.description: Having impaired or defective vision; used figuratively for lacking insight.

brute force.description: Physical strength, as opposed to intelligence or strategy.

the rabbit.description: A clever rabbit who devises a plan to outwit Numskull and save the animals.

Brahma.description: A Hindu god mentioned as one who cannot see the end of clever deceit.

Scripture.description: Refers to sacred Hindu texts that provide moral and ethical guidance.

Rama-with-the-axe.description: A reference to Parashurama, an incarnation of Vishnu known for wielding an axe.

obeisance.description: A gesture of respect or submission, such as bowing.

proverb.description: A short, well-known saying expressing a general truth.

sustenance.description: Means of sustaining life; nourishment or food.

fortress.description: A stronghold or fortified place, often used for defense.

palm-fruit.description: The fruit of a palm tree, referenced in an Indian proverb.

discus.description: A circular weapon (chakra) associated with the god Vishnu.

princess.description: A female royal, referenced in the context of a story.

Sugarcane City.description: The city where the main events of the story take place.

Hiranyakashipu.description: A demon king in Hindu mythology, slain by Vishnu.

Kansa.description: A tyrant king and enemy of Krishna (an avatar of Vishnu) in Hindu mythology.

Madhu.description: A demon in Hindu mythology, slain by Vishnu.

Kaitabha.description: Another demon in Hindu mythology, slain by Vishnu.

conversaziones.description: Social gatherings for conversation, often with intellectual or artistic focus.

betel-leaves.description: Leaves of the betel plant, commonly chewed in India for their stimulant effects.

camphor.description: An aromatic substance used in Indian rituals and perfumes.

aloes.description: Aromatic substances used for fragrance and incense in Indian culture.

musk.description: A fragrant substance used in perfumes, often referenced in Indian literature.

warrior caste.description: Refers to the Kshatriya varna in the traditional Hindu social hierarchy.

the holy law.description: Refers to Dharma or religious law in Hindu tradition.

triple staff.description: A reference to the staff carried by certain Hindu ascetics (tridanda).

stucco.description: A fine plaster used for coating wall surfaces or molding into architectural decorations.

bosom.description: An archaic term for a woman's chest or breasts.

maid.description: An archaic term for a young unmarried woman.

diadem.description: A jeweled crown or headband worn as a symbol of sovereignty.

benediction.description: A blessing, often given during religious ceremonies.

auspicious.description: Conducive to success; favorable or fortunate.

largess.description: Generous gifts, often of money or valuables.

chaplains.description: Clergy attached to a private chapel, institution, or military unit.

retainers.description: Servants or followers of a noble or royal person.

tribute.description: A payment made periodically by one state or ruler to another, especially as a sign of dependence.

contrivance.description: A device or machine skillfully made for a particular purpose.

saffron-scented.description: Refers to the fragrance of saffron, a prized spice used in Indian rituals and cuisine.

mace.description: A heavy club, often used as a weapon and symbol of authority in Indian epics.

yellow pigment.description: Often refers to turmeric or sandalwood paste used in Hindu rituals.

mustard.description: Black mustard seeds, used in Indian rituals for their auspicious qualities.

water-lily.description: A flower symbolizing purity and beauty in Indian literature.

twilight.description: The time of day between sunset and darkness, often used poetically.

monkey.description: An animal trapped in a well, saved by the Brahman, who later provides him with fruit.

goldsmith.description: A man trapped in a well, saved by the Brahman, who later betrays him to the king.

queen.description: The king's wife, who is bitten by the snake and cured by the Brahman.

impale.description: To pierce with a sharp stake, often as a form of execution.

expiation.description: The act of making amends or reparation for guilt or wrongdoing.

conjurer.description: A person who performs magic or sorcery.

avarice.description: Extreme greed for wealth or material gain.

carnivore.description: An animal that feeds on flesh.

grass-nibbler.description: A term for a herbivorous animal, such as an ox or deer.

privy counselor.description: A high-ranking advisor to a king or ruler.

refrain.description: A repeated phrase or comment, often expressing complaint.

merit.description: Spiritual credit or virtue accumulated through good deeds.

sainthood.description: The state of being recognized as a saint, or exceptionally virtuous.

wrought.description: Shaped or fashioned, especially referring to metalwork.

shrine.description: A place regarded as holy due to its association with a divinity or saint.

Leap.description: A flea who drifts into the king's bed and wishes to feed on the king's blood, seeking Creep's permission.

Gangetic.description: Referring to the Ganges River, a major and sacred river in India.

Holy Trinity.description: In Hinduism, refers to the triad of Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva.

cubiculary.description: Relating to a bedroom or sleeping chamber.

viands.description: Foods or provisions, especially of a choice or delicate kind.

unctuous.description: Rich, oily, or greasy in texture or appearance.

au courant.description: A French phrase meaning up to date or well-informed.

crevice.description: A narrow opening or crack, especially in a surface.

nap.description: The raised, fuzzy surface on certain kinds of fabric.

parish.description: An archaic spelling of 'perish', meaning to die.

dyer.description: A person whose occupation is to dye cloth or other materials.

indigo.description: A deep blue dye derived from plants, commonly used in India.

vat.description: A large container used for holding liquids, especially in dyeing.

sage.description: A wise person, often used to refer to revered figures in Indian tradition.

sandal-trees.description: Trees that produce fragrant sandalwood, culturally significant in India.

lotus.description: A water lily, symbolically important in Indian culture and literature.

crocodiles.description: Large aquatic reptiles, often appearing in Indian fables.

saints.description: Holy or virtuous persons, often referenced in Indian literature.

owl.description: A bird who visits Passion, praises his virtues, and later invites him to his home, Lotus Grove.

archer.description: A skilled bowman in the commercial caravan who kills the swan by aiming at sound.

Lotus Grove.description: The home of the owl, described as a pleasant and inviting place.

conch.description: A large seashell used as a ceremonial horn in Indian culture.

herbivorous.description: Describing an animal that eats only plants.

mountebank.description: An archaic term for a trickster or swindler.

caravan.description: A group of travelers, often merchants, journeying together for safety.

abjectly.description: In a manner showing humiliation or submissiveness.

slanders.description: False and damaging statements about someone.

leopard.description: One of Haughty's followers, who offers his life to the lion during their starvation.

exotic.description: Something foreign or unusual, not native to the area.

unguipugnacious.description: A rare or coined term, likely meaning 'not given to fighting with claws'; used to indicate animals of the same family.

sacrifieer.description: An archaic spelling of 'sacrificer', meaning one who offers a sacrifice.

dependents.description: Those who rely on someone else for support, especially subjects of a king.

vulture.description: A bird of prey, used metaphorically for a type of adviser in the story.

swans.description: Birds used metaphorically for wise or noble advisers in the story.

anjana.description: A type of tree whose wood is cut by the carpenter; refers to a specific kind of timber in Indian forests.

dainty.description: A delicacy; something delicious or choice to eat.

chewers.description: Likely refers to a type of food or sweetmeat meant for chewing, possibly betel or similar Indian snacks.

grapejuice.description: Juice made from grapes, used as a flavoring in food.

tidbit.description: A small and particularly tasty piece of food.

scurvy trick.description: An old-fashioned phrase meaning a mean or underhanded action.

prosperous.description: Favorable or promising, often referring to good fortune.

elide.description: To erase or remove; in this context, to wear away.

sacrificial trial.description: A ritual act of sacrifice, often for religious or spiritual purposes.

extremis.description: A Latin phrase meaning in extreme circumstances or at the point of death.

foeman.description: An archaic term for an enemy or opponent.

strife.description: An archaic English word meaning conflict or struggle.

judicious.description: Possessing sound judgment; wise and prudent.

boastings.description: Archaic or formal term for acts of boasting or bragging.

heaven.description: Used here to refer to the sky or upper atmosphere, often with spiritual or cultural connotations in Indian literature.

ganders.description: Male geese; used here to describe Shell-Neck's two bird friends.

vicissitudes.description: Changes or variations, typically referring to the unpredictable changes in life.

atmosphere.description: The air or sky, often used in a literary or scientific sense.

thrive.description: To prosper or flourish, used here in a proverbial sense.

cognate.description: Related or connected, often by origin or nature.

nursery.description: A place where young animals or birds are cared for; here, refers to the place where the plover's eggs were kept.

meshes.description: The openings or spaces in a net.

counsel.description: Advice or guidance, especially from someone wise or experienced.

fig tree.description: A type of tree, significant in Indian culture and often featured in fables.

lotus-face.description: A poetic term from Indian literature describing a face as beautiful as a lotus flower.

dullard.description: An archaic term for a slow-witted or foolish person.

sacrifice.description: A religious ritual involving offerings to deities, common in Hindu tradition.

firefly.description: A bioluminescent insect, mistaken for fire by the monkeys.

arboreal.description: Living in or related to trees.

worse-born.description: A term from Indian tradition referring to a son who is morally inferior to his parents.

well-trained.description: In this context, refers to minds that are educated or cultivated, often used in Indian philosophical discourse.

dinars.description: A historical currency, likely referring to gold coins used in ancient India and other regions.

mimosa.description: A type of tree mentioned as the hiding place for Wrong-Mind's father; native to India and known for its sensitive leaves.

mungoose.description: A small carnivorous mammal native to South Asia, referenced in a proverb within the story.

ordeal.description: A trial or test, often by physical means, used in ancient times to determine guilt or innocence.

magistrates.description: Officials who administer the law, typically judges or local authorities.

lucre.description: Archaic term for money or profit, often with a negative connotation.

dictum.description: A formal pronouncement or authoritative statement.

bail.description: A sum of money or guarantee given to ensure someone's appearance in court.

Wrong-Mind’s father.description: Hidden by Wrong-Mind in the mimosa tree to falsely accuse Right-Mind, but is exposed and confesses the truth.

scamp.description: An archaic term for a mischievous or dishonest person.

oversubtle.description: Excessively or unnecessarily subtle or clever.

circumspection.description: Cautiousness or careful consideration of all circumstances.

adamant.description: A legendary rock or mineral to which many, often contradictory, properties were ascribed, used here to mean unbreakable or extremely hard.

calumniator.description: One who makes false and defamatory statements; a slanderer.

pals.description: An old-fashioned word for friends or companions.

Naduk.description: A merchant who loses his money, travels abroad, and later returns to reclaim his iron balance-beam.

Lakshman.description: A merchant in Naduk's town who is entrusted with the iron balance-beam and later claims it was eaten by mice.

Money-God.description: Lakshman's son, who is sent with Naduk to the river and is hidden in a cave as part of Naduk's ruse.

palace.description: Refers to the royal residence or seat of authority where disputes are brought for judgment.

King.description: A reference to the ruler, mentioned in the context of Cheek's story.

hermits.description: Ascetic individuals who live in seclusion for spiritual reasons, referenced in a story told by Cheek.

Beef-eaters.description: A term used to describe people who eat beef, referenced in a story to contrast different upbringings.

balance-beam.description: A large beam used as a scale for weighing, here made of iron and used as a valuable item.

pawn.description: To deposit an item as security for a loan or obligation.

dunderhead.description: An archaic English term meaning a fool or stupid person.

meretricious.description: Describes something or someone that is superficially attractive but lacks real value; often used to describe women of questionable virtue.

consort.description: To associate or keep company with.

litigation.description: The process of taking legal action or resolving disputes in court.

hen-parrot.description: A mother parrot who brings two chicks into the world on a mountain.

parrot.description: Refers to both parrot chicks, one raised by hunters and one by holy men, each displaying different behaviors due to their upbringing.

hermitage.description: A secluded dwelling or retreat where holy men live, often in the forest.

holy men.description: Ascetics or sages who live a life of religious devotion, often in hermitages.

repose.description: Rest or relaxation, especially in a peaceful setting.

robber.description: A thief or bandit, referenced in the proverb.

prince.description: The son of a king who dislikes traditional royal pursuits and sets out on a journey with his friends.

merchant’s son.description: A friend of the prince, practical and focused on acquiring wealth.

son of a man of learning.description: A friend of the prince, the son of a counselor, known for his cleverness.

chief.description: The head of the Bhil village who can interpret the songs of birds and detains the travelers.

thief.description: A fellow traveler who plots to steal the gems but ultimately sacrifices himself to save the others.

Climbing Mountain.description: A specific mountain mentioned as a place where precious gems can be found.

Bhil.description: An indigenous tribal community in India, referenced here as villagers in the jungle.

equitation.description: The art or practice of horse riding.

aviary.description: A large enclosure for keeping birds.

loincloths.description: A single piece of cloth wrapped around the hips, traditional attire in some parts of India.

dungeon.description: An underground prison cell, often used for holding captives.

Book I.description: The first section of the Panchatantra, titled 'The Loss of Friends.'

secretary of the treasury.description: An official responsible for managing the kingdom's finances.

arbor.description: A shaded area in a garden, often formed by trees or climbing plants.

magistrate.description: A civil officer or judge who administers the law.

altruist.description: A person who is selflessly concerned for the well-being of others.

multiform.description: Having many forms, shapes, or appearances.

ch-33: son of a man of learning
